Subject: Post-demo model shortlist + cost/latency/quality tradeoffs

Hi Jordan — thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap + the recommended model shortlist based on what we saw (search/QA + structured extraction, 300ms P50 target, strict hallucination tolerance):

Summary / next steps
- I'm attaching the shortlist and prompt set we discussed and a snapshot of the benchmark run. Please share any additional sample prompts and a small eval set (50‑100 examples) so we can run a tailored POC.
- Proposed next step: grant eval access to our sandbox (<2 business days), run your sample prompt set, then a 2‑week canary on your traffic profile.

Recommended shortlist (rationale follows)
1) redwood-instruct-rlhf-13B (default) — balance of cost and quality
   - Rationale: strong instruction-following; P50 ~180–230ms on Dedicated A100-ish hardware, P95 ~420–650ms. Lowest token cost among the shortlisted models. Good fit if you want to iterate quickly and keep cost predictable.
   - Unit cost (hosted, observed): ~$120 per 1M tokens (generation + context), good for conversational/QA workloads.

2) Llama-2-70B (FP16, quantized) — highest quality but higher latency/cost
   - Rationale: best hallucination resilience in our open-model benchmarks for long context extractions. P50 ~420–520ms; P95 ~900–1200ms on dense GPU setups. Recommend for high-accuracy fields where mistakes are costly.
   - Unit cost (hosted, observed): ~$620 per 1M tokens (depends on quantization and deployment settings).

3) redwood-qa-7B (low-latency variant) — low-latency, cheaper but watch for edge-case regressions
   - Rationale: Excellent P50 (<120ms) and low per-token cost (~$45 per 1M tokens). Slight drop in long-context extraction exact-match vs 13B/70B; good candidate for latency-first endpoints and front-door reranking.

Attachments included:
- shortlist-v1.pdf (shortlist + quick rationale)
- acme-prompt-set.jsonl (sample prompt set we used to benchmark)
- benchmark-report-0304.pdf (aggregated metrics)

Links:
- Shared eval folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDEF-acme-eval
- HubSpot deal: https://app.redwood.com/hubspot/ACME-2345

Open questions for you:
- Do you want to prioritize latency above cost (>=300ms P50 target) or quality above all?
- Can you share the small eval set (50–100 samples) we discussed?

I'll loop Marcus (SE) on the technical tradeoffs for latency/cost and to propose a quantization plan.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Jordan — quick technical notes for the three shortlisted options and answers to your specific questions. Quoting key bits below.

On Thu, 5 Mar 2026 at 08:11 AM Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-analytics.com> wrote:
> Latency SLO: we target ~300ms P50 at peak for our inline QA endpoint. If 13B hits P50 ~180–230ms that looks good, but what do you expect at our traffic profile (bursts to 200 qps)?

Short answer on traffic/latency: with continuous batching and the right autoscale curve, 13B (redwood-instruct-rlhf-13B) should sustain ~200 qps P50 in the ~200–280ms range on dedicated T4v3/GPU pools with burst capacity. Key caveats:
- Warm KV cache is critical for short prompts — cold-cache starts will see higher P50.
- P95 will spike during autoscale transitions; we generally recommend a small burst reserve (20–30%) for that traffic profile.

On hallucination/regression risk: we run targeted prompt-set evals (exact-match + entity F1) and a human review sample. Observations from our benchmark (attached synthetic-bench-results.csv):
- redwood-qa-7B: entity-F1 ~0.82, EM ~0.69 (good latency, minor edge-case regressions on long extractions)
- redwood-instruct-rlhf-13B: entity-F1 ~0.88, EM ~0.78 (best cost/quality balance in open benchmarks)
- Llama-2-70B (quantized): entity-F1 ~0.91, EM ~0.84 (best quality, highest cost and latency)

Economics (hosted observed; Dedicated reserved reduces delta):
- 7B hosted: ~$45 / 1M tokens
- 13B hosted: ~$120 / 1M tokens
- 70B hosted (quantized): ~$620 / 1M tokens
- Dedicated (reserved): expect ~20–40% lower per-token serving cost depending on commit and utilization. We can run a quick utilization simulation if you share expected qps and retention.

Recommended canary approach:
1) Start with 13B in hosted sandbox using your 75-example eval set — validate EM/F1 and latency at small scale (2–3 hours).
2) If quality meets threshold, run a 48–72 hour canary on live traffic with autoscale + 30% burst capacity. Monitor token-cost delta.
3) If you need higher accuracy for a subset of calls (e.g., high-risk extraction), route those to 70B model as a fallback via our smart routing policy. This hybrid reduces overall cost while preserving quality for critical calls.

We can provision sandbox access within 24 business hours after you upload the eval set to the shared folder. I'll attach the synthetic microbench CSV from today's run for reference.

Cheers,
Marcus
